chapterNote: An acrostic wisdom psalm of David: successive sections begin with successive letters of the Hebrew alphabet. Three refrains anchor it — 'do not fret' (charah, vv. 1,7,8), 'inherit the land' (yarash, vv. 9,11,22,29,34), and the contrast of the wicked's end with the future of the righteous.

1.text: Do not burn with anger over evildoers, and do not envy those who do wrong.
1.amp: Do not burn with anger [charah — work yourself into a heated fret] over evildoers, and do not envy those who do wrong [don't let their success kindle resentment in you].
1.notes: charah (H2734) = to burn/be kindled — 'fret' is heated agitation; this is the psalm's opening refrain, recurring at vv. 7 and 8.

2.text: For like grass they will soon be cut down, and wither like the green plant.
2.amp: For like grass they will soon be cut down [their flourishing has no permanence], and wither like the green plant [green today, mown and dry tomorrow].
2.notes: The wicked's prosperity is grass — fast-growing, shallow-rooted, soon cut and faded (nabel, H5034).

3.text: Trust in the LORD and do good; settle in the land and pasture yourself on His faithfulness.
3.amp: Trust in the LORD and do good; settle in the land [dwell secure where He has placed you] and pasture yourself on His faithfulness [feed, as a flock feeds, on His sure care].
3.notes: batach (H982) = to trust/lean on; the closing line plays on ra'ah (feed/shepherd) with 'emunah (H530, faithfulness): 'feed on His faithfulness' / 'graze in safety.'

4.text: Take exquisite delight in the LORD, and He will give you the desires of your heart — for when He Himself becomes your joy, He both shapes and satisfies what your heart most wants.
4.amp: Take exquisite delight in the LORD [anag — luxuriate in Him, make the LORD your supreme gladness], and He will give you the desires of your heart [mish'alot — both the longings He plants there when He is your treasure, and their fulfillment].
4.notes: anag (H6026) = to be soft / take exquisite, luxuriant delight; mish'alot (H4862) = the heart's petitions/requests. The deep sense: delighting in God reshapes the heart's desires toward what He delights to give.

5.text: Roll your way onto the LORD — commit the whole road of your life to Him; lean your trust on Him, and He Himself will bring it to pass.
5.amp: Roll your way onto the LORD [galal — roll the whole burden of your path off your own shoulders onto His]; lean your trust on Him, and He Himself will bring it to pass [He will see it through].
5.notes: galal (H1556) = to roll; KJV margin: 'Roll thy way upon.' Commit by rolling the load off yourself onto the LORD (cf. Prov 16:3).

6.text: He will bring out your righteousness like the dawn, and your just cause like the noonday sun.
6.amp: He will bring out your righteousness like the dawn [vindicating you in plain sight], and your just cause like the noonday sun [blazing, undeniable, at its height].
6.notes: Vindication imagery: hidden righteousness brought into full daylight; mishpat (H4941) here = one's just cause / vindication.

7.text: Rest in the LORD and wait for Him in patient hope; do not let it burn in you when the schemer thrives along his way, when a man pushes his wicked plots through to success.
7.amp: Rest in the LORD [damam — fall silent, quiet your restless striving] and wait for Him in patient hope; do not let it burn in you [charah — the heated fret] when the schemer thrives along his way, when a man pushes his wicked plots through to success.
7.notes: damam (H1826) = to be silent/still (KJV margin: 'Be silent to') — quiet submission, not anxious activity; the 'fret' refrain (charah) returns.

8.text: Let go of anger, and leave wrath behind; do not fret — it leads a man only into evil.
8.amp: Let go of anger [raphah — release your grip on it], and leave wrath behind; do not fret — it leads a man only into evil [resentment, left to burn, breeds wrongdoing].
8.notes: raphah (H7503) = to let drop / relax one's hold; the verse warns that fretting itself becomes a doorway to evildoing.

9.text: For evildoers will be cut off, but those who wait for the LORD will inherit the land.
9.amp: For evildoers will be cut off [karat — severed, removed], but those who wait for the LORD [qavah — wait with taut, hopeful expectation] will inherit the land [the promised inheritance — the refrain of this psalm].
9.notes: yarash (H3423), 'inherit the land,' is the psalm's refrain (vv. 9,11,22,29,34); qavah (H6960) = to wait with tense hope.

10.text: Yet a little while, and the wicked man is gone; you will search the place where he stood, and he will not be there.
10.amp: Yet a little while, and the wicked man is gone; you will search the place where he stood [scanning where he once towered], and he will not be there [vanished without a trace].
10.notes: The wicked's permanence is an illusion — 'a little while,' and the search for him comes up empty.

11.text: But the humble will inherit the land and luxuriate in the fullness of peace.
11.amp: But the humble [anav — the lowly and bowed-down, not the self-asserting] will inherit the land and luxuriate [anag — the same exquisite delight as verse 4] in the fullness of peace [shalom — wholeness, not the mere absence of conflict].
11.notes: anav (H6035) = humble/lowly. Jesus cites this verse in Matt 5:5 ('the meek shall inherit the earth'); 'luxuriate' echoes anag of v.4; shalom (H7965) = full well-being.

12.text: The wicked man plots against the righteous, gnashing at him with his teeth in open hatred.
12.amp: The wicked man plots against the righteous [zamam — schemes with deliberate intent], gnashing at him with his teeth in open hatred [bared, animal hostility].
12.notes: zamam (H2161) = to devise/scheme; teeth-grinding pictures raw, predatory hatred.

13.text: The Lord only laughs at him, for He sees that his day of reckoning is already on its way.
13.amp: The Lord only laughs at him [the scheming is absurd before God], for He sees that his day of reckoning is already on its way [the appointed day is fixed].
13.notes: Heb. 'Adonai (H136), 'the Lord' (sovereign Master) — distinct from YHWH (LORD); 'his day' = the day of judgment fixed for the wicked.

14.text: The wicked unsheathe the sword and string the bow, to cast down the poor and needy, and to butcher those who walk uprightly.
14.amp: The wicked unsheathe the sword and string the bow [armed and ready for violence], to cast down the poor and needy, and to butcher [tabach — slaughter as one butchers an animal] those who walk uprightly.
14.notes: tabach (H2873) = to slaughter/butcher; the targets are the defenseless ('poor and needy') and the morally straight ('the upright of way').

15.text: But their sword will pierce their own heart, and their bows will be shattered.
15.amp: But their sword will pierce their own heart [the violence recoils on the one who wields it], and their bows will be shattered.
15.notes: Poetic justice: the weapons of the wicked turn back on themselves (shabar, H7665 = to break in pieces).

16.text: Better the little that the righteous has than the abundance of many wicked.
16.amp: Better the little that the righteous has [enough, held with God] than the abundance of many wicked [riches without Him, soon to be broken — see v.17].
16.notes: A wisdom 'better-than' saying: covenant 'little' outweighs godless 'much.'

17.text: The wicked will have their arms broken — their strength shattered — while the LORD Himself holds the righteous upright.
17.amp: The wicked will have their arms broken [their strength — 'arm' — snapped], while the LORD Himself holds the righteous upright [samak — props up, holds firm].
17.notes: 'Arm' (zeroa, H2220) = strength/power; samak (H5564) = to lean/uphold — God is the support the wicked's own strength is not.

18.text: The LORD watches over the days of those who walk in integrity, and the inheritance they receive endures forever.
18.amp: The LORD watches over [yada — knows with intimate, caring attention] the days of those who walk in integrity [tamim — whole and sound], and the inheritance they receive endures forever [olam — into the ages].
18.notes: yada (H3045) = intimate, caring knowledge; tamim (H8549) = whole/blameless; the nachalah (inheritance) endures olam (forever).

19.text: They will not be disgraced when disaster comes, and in the days of famine they will eat their fill.
19.amp: They will not be disgraced when disaster comes [when calamity falls on all], and in the days of famine they will eat their fill [saba — satisfied and full, while others starve].
19.notes: saba (H7646) = to be satisfied/filled; the righteous are provisioned precisely when scarcity exposes the wicked.

20.text: But the wicked will perish; the enemies of the LORD, like the brief beauty of the fields, will soon be scorched — going up in smoke and consumed away.
20.amp: But the wicked will perish; the enemies of the LORD, like the brief beauty of the fields [the fleeting splendor of green pasture], will soon be scorched — going up in smoke and consumed away [as fleeting as sunburned grass or rising smoke].
20.notes: A difficult line; Heb. plays on yaqar (preciousness/glory) and kar (pastures): the wicked's splendor is as fleeting as sunburned grass or rising smoke; kalah (H3615), 'consume,' is repeated for emphasis.

21.text: The wicked takes a loan and never returns it, but the righteous one is gracious and keeps on giving.
21.amp: The wicked takes a loan and never returns it [taking without returning], but the righteous one is gracious and keeps on giving [chanan — open-handed favor that asks nothing back].
21.notes: Contrast of character: the wicked is a taker who defaults; the righteous reflects God's grace (chanan, H2603) by giving.

22.text: For those He blesses will inherit the land, but those He curses will be cut off.
22.amp: For those He blesses will inherit the land [the blessing carries the inheritance with it], but those He curses will be cut off [severed from it].
22.notes: The inheritance refrain again, framed by divine blessing (barak, H1288) versus curse (qalal, H7043).

23.text: The steps of a man are made firm by the LORD, and He delights in his way.
23.amp: The steps of a man are made firm by the LORD [kun — established, set steady], and He delights in his way [God Himself takes pleasure in the path of the one He steadies].
23.notes: kun (H3559) = to establish/make firm; note that it is the LORD who delights (chaphets) in the man's way — a mutual delight (cf. v.4).

24.text: Though he stumbles, he will not be hurled headlong, for the LORD holds him up by the hand.
24.amp: Though he stumbles, he will not be hurled headlong [he may fall, but not to ruin], for the LORD holds him up by the hand [samak — He grips and steadies him].
24.notes: naphal (fall, H5307) versus tul (be hurled down, H2904): the righteous may stumble but is not destroyed — God's hand (yad) holds (samak) him.

25.text: I have been young, and now I am old, yet I have never seen the righteous forsaken or his children begging bread.
25.amp: I have been young, and now I am old, yet I have never seen the righteous forsaken [abandoned by God to ruin] or his children begging bread [a lifetime's witness to God's faithful provision].
25.notes: David's testimony from long experience; azab (H5800) = to forsake/abandon — the righteous are never finally abandoned.

26.text: All day long he deals kindly and lends freely, and his offspring are blessed because of him.
26.amp: All day long he deals kindly and lends freely [generous as a settled habit, not a passing mood], and his offspring are blessed because of him [the open hand leaves a legacy].
26.notes: Echoes v.21: the righteous gives (chanan); his generosity blesses the next generation.

27.text: Depart from evil and do good, and you will settle in the land secure forever.
27.amp: Depart from evil and do good [the two-sided command: forsake, and pursue], and you will settle in the land secure forever [at home, for good].
27.notes: sur (H5493) = to turn aside from; the wisdom path is negative (turn from evil) and positive (do good) together.

28.text: For the LORD loves justice and never abandons His faithful ones; they are kept safe forever, but the offspring of the wicked are cut off.
28.amp: For the LORD loves justice and never abandons His faithful ones [chasidim — those bound to Him in covenant love]; they are kept safe forever [shamar — guarded, watched over], but the offspring of the wicked are cut off.
28.notes: chasid (H2623) = the covenant-faithful (linked to chesed); shamar (H8104) = to guard/keep — God's preservation of His own.

29.text: It is the righteous who will take the land as their inheritance, settling in it for all time.
29.amp: It is the righteous who will take the land as their inheritance, settling in it for all time [the refrain restated as settled fact].
29.notes: The inheritance refrain (vv. 9,11,22,34); shakan (H7931) = to settle/dwell; 'ad (H5703) = perpetuity — 'for all time.'

30.text: The mouth of the righteous murmurs wisdom, and his tongue speaks what is just.
30.amp: The mouth of the righteous murmurs wisdom [hagah — the same word as 'meditate' in Psalm 1:2; what he chews on within now overflows in speech], and his tongue speaks what is just.
30.notes: hagah (H1897) here ties back to Ps 1:2: the law meditated (chewed) within becomes wisdom spoken without.

31.text: The law of his God is held within his heart; not one of his steps gives way.
31.amp: The law of his God is held within his heart [internalized, not merely external]; not one of his steps gives way [maad — no loss of footing, because the law steadies them].
31.notes: torah in the heart (cf. Jer 31:33) yields steady steps; maad (H4571) = to slip/totter.

32.text: The wicked lies in wait for the righteous, seeking to kill him.
32.amp: The wicked lies in wait for the righteous [tsaphah — watches like a hunter for the moment], seeking to kill him.
32.notes: tsaphah (H6822) = to lie in wait / keep watch — predatory surveillance.

33.text: The LORD will not leave him in his enemy's grip, nor let him be declared guilty when he is dragged into court.
33.amp: The LORD will not leave him in his enemy's grip, nor let him be declared guilty when he is dragged into court [though men judge him, God has the final verdict].
33.notes: Even when the righteous is dragged before a hostile court, God will not leave (azab) him to the wicked or ratify a guilty verdict.

34.text: Wait for the LORD and keep His way, and He will raise you up to inherit the land; when the wicked are cut off, you will see it.
34.amp: Wait for the LORD [qavah — hopeful, expectant waiting] and keep His way, and He will raise you up [rum — lift you to honor] to inherit the land; when the wicked are cut off, you will see it [you will outlast them and witness the outcome].
34.notes: Gathers the psalm's commands: wait (qavah, vv. 7,9), keep (shamar), inherit (yarash). rum (H7311) = to lift up/exalt.

35.text: I have watched a wicked man, ruthless and overbearing, towering and spreading himself like a green tree rooted in its native soil.
35.amp: I have watched a wicked man, ruthless and overbearing [arits — tyrannical, in full power], towering and spreading himself like a green tree rooted in its native soil [deep-rooted, seemingly unassailable].
35.notes: arits (H6184) = ruthless/tyrannical; the wicked looks like a thriving native tree — set against the next verse.

36.text: Yet he passed away, and there he was — gone; I searched for him, but he could not be found.
36.amp: Yet he passed away, and there he was — gone [the towering tree vanished]; I searched for him, but he could not be found [no root, no trace, nothing left].
36.notes: Deliberate contrast with v.35: the 'native tree' uprooted and gone — echoing the chaff of Psalm 1:4.

37.text: Mark the man of integrity and fix your eyes on the upright, for the man of peace has a future before him.
37.amp: Mark the man of integrity [tam — the blameless] and fix your eyes on the upright, for the man of peace has a future before him [acharith — a latter end, a posterity; his life ends in shalom, not ruin].
37.notes: acharith (H319) = the 'after-part' — destiny/posterity; the blameless has a future, unlike the wicked of v.38.

38.text: But rebels will be destroyed together; the future of the wicked will be cut off.
38.amp: But rebels will be destroyed together [pasha — those in open revolt, swept away as one]; the future of the wicked will be cut off [no acharith, no posterity — the opposite of v.37].
38.notes: pasha (H6586) = to rebel/transgress; their acharith (future, v.37) is precisely what gets 'cut off.'

39.text: The salvation of the righteous comes from the LORD; He is their stronghold in the time of trouble.
39.amp: The salvation of the righteous comes from the LORD [not from themselves]; He is their stronghold [maoz — fortress, refuge] in the time of trouble [tsarah — tight, pressing distress].

40.text: The LORD helps them and rescues them; He rescues them from the wicked and saves them, because they have taken refuge in Him.
40.amp: The LORD helps them and rescues them [palat — brings them to safety]; He rescues them from the wicked and saves them, because they have taken refuge in Him [chasah — fled to Him for shelter: the psalm's final note is not their merit but their refuge].
40.notes: chasah (H2620) = to take refuge / flee for shelter — the psalm ends on trust as refuge; the ground of deliverance is sheltering in the LORD.
